clue.text: In a US city see tailless pack animal

indicators.note: the pack piece is placed in the middle of the city phrase, so 'In' marks the containment

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles

indicators.note: tailless says the last letter of the word pack is cut off

parts.note: a pack is a bundle carried on the back

explanation.surface: A tourist in an American city is told to look at a pack animal that has lost its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pack animal' looks like one phrase, but only 'animal' is the definition; 'see' is a link meaning 'look'. 'tailless' cuts the last letter, and 'In' puts the result inside the city phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The alpaca is a South American domesticated beast related to the llama, kept for its wool.

clue.text: Most pathetic, heading off after pinching your old gemstone

indicators.note: after pinching means having grabbed something, so one piece closes round the other
heading off says the first letter of the word is removed

parts.note: lamest means feeblest, most pathetic
thy is the archaic form of your

explanation.surface: A sorry thief, walking off after stealing your old gemstone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' looks like the thief leaving, but it removes a first letter, leaving AMEST, which then holds the old word for your.
explanation.definitionFit: Amethyst is a violet variety of quartz prized as a semi-precious jewel.

clue.text: Apple and a different fruit, one consumed by chap

parts.note: a pear is a fruit other than an apple

indicators.note: consumed by means eaten, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a chap is a man
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A man eats an apple and a second kind of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consumed by' puts I inside MAN, giving MAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A pearmain is an old variety of eating apple, such as the Worcester Pearmain.

clue.text: Sticks around with individuals going short of nothing

parts.note: CA, short for circa, means around

indicators.note: going short of means doing without, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: ones are single individuals
O is the round figure for nothing

explanation.surface: Some people stay around even though they have nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going short of nothing' drops O from ONES, giving NES.
explanation.definitionFit: Canes are walking sticks or rods, so sticks is a plain synonym.

clue.text: Royal house party rejected? Right

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: Lab is short for Labour, a UK political party
moral means right, ethically proper

explanation.surface: A royal residence's party was turned down; quite right too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns LAB into BAL. BALMORAL is the British royal family's castle in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Balmoral Castle in Aberdeenshire is a private residence of the British monarch.

clue.text: A young man warning about rackets in the Treasury?

parts.note: a lad is a young man
dins are loud noises, rackets
cave, Latin for beware, is old schoolboy slang for a warning

explanation.surface: A young civil servant warns about fraudulent rackets inside the Treasury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' just links the warning to the rackets. Aladdin's cave, from the Arabian Nights tale, holds a fabulous hoard; 'the Treasury' is the government department in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A place stuffed with riches is a treasure-house, which is what a treasury literally is.

clue.text: Speaker stuck in middle of motorway, facing a number of delays?

indicators.note: facing means set next to, so the last piece follows on
stuck in the middle of means placed inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main motorway, written MI
an orator is a public speaker

explanation.surface: A talker stranded mid-motorway faces a whole series of hold-ups.
explanation.walkthrough: MI stands for the M1, a British motorway, with the 1 read as I; 'stuck in middle of' puts ORATOR inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Moratoria are official suspensions or postponements, so several of them are a set of delays.

clue.text: Careless teacher of religion

parts.note: RE is religious education, a school subject
Miss is how pupils address a female teacher

explanation.surface: A slapdash teacher of RE.
explanation.walkthrough: The parts appear in the opposite order to the surface: religion first, then teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: Remiss means negligent in one's duty, a synonym for slack or neglectful.

clue.text: Source of timber left in private room

parts.note: a den is a private retreat or study

explanation.surface: Wood left lying in someone's study.
explanation.definitionFit: The linden, or lime tree, yields a soft pale wood used for carving.

clue.text: Cameron, perhaps, turns to meet Geordie woman

indicators.note: turns means flips round, so the name is read backwards

parts.note: Dave was the nickname of David Cameron, the British prime minister
a Geordie comes from Newcastle, in the North East (NE) of England

explanation.surface: A politician turns up to meet a woman from Newcastle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' makes EVAD from DAVE. A Geordie is a native of Tyneside in the North East of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Evadne is a female name from Greek myth, the wife of Capaneus, so a woman.

clue.text: Mary and Enid working as farmers?

indicators.note: working means being worked into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Two women, Mary and Enid, have jobs on the land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges MARYENID; 'and' is only a link. The question mark flags that these are only certain farmers.
explanation.definitionFit: Dairymen are farmers who keep cows for milk, an example of farmers.

clue.text: Communist writer gets allowance for makeover

parts.note: Red is a familiar name for a communist
Umberto Eco was an Italian novelist
a ration is a fixed allowance

explanation.surface: A left-wing author receives money to have his image overhauled.
explanation.definitionFit: Redecoration is renewing a room's paint and furnishings, a makeover for a home.

clue.text: A politician's time in main part of London

indicators.note: in places the politician pieces inside the other word

parts.note: head means main or chief, as in head office
an MP is a Member of Parliament; the 's adds S

explanation.surface: An MP's term in office in the heart of the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'main part' looks like the container, but 'part of London' is the definition and 'main' alone is the outer word. Hampstead is a district in north London.
explanation.definitionFit: Hampstead is a north London district known for its heath, so a portion of the city.

clue.text: Sample part of banquet — a steak

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Trying a bit of a feast: a steak.
explanation.definitionFit: To sample food is to try a little of it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Terribly bad trainers tethering new dog

indicators.note: tethering means tying in, so one piece holds the other
terribly means done badly, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Poor dog-handlers trying to tie up a young dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terribly' rearranges BADTRAINERS to SAINTBERARD; 'tethering' holds N inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The St Bernard is a large Alpine breed famed for mountain rescue.

clue.text: Play doctor wrote without help

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so one piece wraps the other
to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a hand is help, as in lend a hand

explanation.surface: A medic wrote a stage play unaided.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without help' reads as one phrase meaning unaided, but 'without' here has its old sense of outside, and 'help' is the piece it surrounds; 'doctor' rearranges the letters of 'wrote'.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-hander is a stage drama with only two actors, so a kind of drama.

clue.text: A thin lad abandoned country

indicators.note: abandoned means wild and unrestrained, so the letters run riot

explanation.surface: A skinny boy has left his homeland.
explanation.definitionFit: Thailand is a nation in South-East Asia.

clue.text: Agreed when children might absorb religious work

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as he left'

indicators.note: absorb means take in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: seed means offspring, children
NT is the New Testament

explanation.surface: Consent given at a time children might soak up some scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'children' as offspring is the old sense of seed; 'might' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Assented means consented or went along with, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Carrying something that burns endlessly, medic sets fire to buses

parts.note: MO is a medical officer

indicators.note: carrying means holding, so one word contains the other

parts.note: torches means sets alight

indicators.note: endlessly says the last letter is lost

parts.note: coal is a fuel that burns

explanation.surface: A doctor commits arson on a bus while carrying burning material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' trims COAL to COA, which TORCHES carries: TOR-COA-CHES.
explanation.definitionFit: Motor coaches are long-distance buses, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Small room's oppressive temperature

parts.note: close weather is humid and oppressive

explanation.surface: A tiny room is stuffy and too warm.
explanation.definitionFit: A closet is a cupboard or small private chamber.

clue.text: Racing driver that at Le Mans enters refuelling area

indicators.note: enters means goes in, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: the pit is where racing cars refuel
que is French for that; Le Mans is a French racing town

explanation.surface: A driver at the Le Mans race pulls into the pit lane.
explanation.definitionFit: Nelson Piquet was a Brazilian Formula One world champion driver.

clue.text: The French girl oddly lacking a name

parts.note: le is French for the

indicators.note: oddly lacking means the odd letters are dropped, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: A French girl strangely has no name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly lacking' keeps only the 2nd and 4th letters of 'girl', I and L. 'girl' wants to be the definition, but 'name' is.
explanation.definitionFit: Leila is a female given name of Arabic origin.

clue.text: Publicise reissue of a Verdi set

indicators.note: a reissue is a new version, so the letters are put out again in a new order

explanation.surface: Promoting a re-release of a boxed set of Verdi operas.
explanation.definitionFit: To advertise is to promote or make known publicly.

clue.text: Representative section of free verse

indicators.note: section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A typical stretch of poetry without rhyme or metre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Representative' reads as an adjective (typical), but it is a noun: an official.
explanation.definitionFit: A reeve was a local official acting for a lord or the Crown, a deputy or agent.

clue.text: Soldier did manoeuvres in quadrangle ignoring regimental leader

indicators.note: in places the shuffled letters inside the other word
ignoring means leaving out a letter

parts.note: a square is a quadrangle

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of the following word
manoeuvres means moves about, so the letters are shifted

explanation.surface: A private drilled on the barracks square, without his commanding officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regimental leader' looks like an officer, but it is just the letter R; 'manoeuvres' rearranges 'did', and 'in' puts that inside the shortened square word.
explanation.definitionFit: Squaddie is British slang for a private soldier.

clue.text: Meal with no end of wine after theatre

indicators.note: after means the next piece follows the theatre word

parts.note: rep is repertory theatre

indicators.note: no end of means the final letter is removed

parts.note: Asti is a sparkling Italian wine

explanation.surface: Dinner after the show, but with the wine nearly gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end of' trims ASTI to AST. 'with no end of' sounds like 'plenty of', but it means a letter is cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A repast is a formal word for a meal.

clue.text: Teaching noted mathematician about origins of theorems, oddly

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: Alan Turing was a famous British mathematician

indicators.note: origins of means the first letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A famous mathematician gives lessons on the beginnings of theorems, strangely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' looks like an anagram signal, but it only gives its first letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutoring is private instruction, a form of teaching.

clue.text: Male journalists given notice?

parts.note: he is the male pronoun
two editors, each written ED

explanation.surface: A man and his reporters received their notice of dismissal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given notice' suggests being sacked; read it as paid notice to.
explanation.definitionFit: To heed something is to take notice of it, so heeded means attention was paid.
